display.text: Model property in which predictor contributions add together and a predictor's slope does not depend on other predictors' values.
Version of R² that accounts for the number of predictors relative to sample size, aiding comparisons of models with differing complexity.
Correlation between errors from observations ordered in time or another sequence. Also called serial correlation.
Representation of a k-category predictor with k − 1 binary indicators and a reference category in a model with an intercept. Also called indicator coding.
Unobserved difference between a response and its population model mean, representing variation unexplained by the predictors. Notation: ε.
Error variance that changes across predictor values, often suggested by widening or narrowing residual spread.
Constant error variance across predictor values; residual plots assess whether the spread is roughly stable.
Assumption that errors from different observations are independent; serially related errors violate it.
Assumption that the conditional mean response is represented by the specified linear combination of predictors.
Inaccuracy in recorded predictor values that can bias estimated regression relationships.
Strong linear relationships among predictors that make separate coefficient effects difficult to estimate precisely.
Model for a quantitative response using two or more predictors: Y = β₀ + β₁X₁ + … + βₖXₖ + ε.
Display comparing a residual distribution with a normal reference; points near a reference diagonal support approximate normality. The text discusses P-P and Q-Q versions.
Assumption of normally distributed model errors used for conventional small-sample inference; assessed approximately through residual distributions.
Test of whether the predictors collectively add linear explanatory information beyond an intercept-only model; its null sets all predictor slopes to zero.
Exact linear dependence among predictors that prevents unique estimation of all coefficients.
Proportion of response variation explained by a fitted least-squares model with an intercept; higher values indicate closer fit to the observed data. Notation: R².
Category represented by zeros on all dummy variables, against which the other category coefficients are interpreted.
Expected change in the response per one-unit increase in a predictor, holding the other predictors fixed in an additive linear model.
Observed response minus its fitted value; residuals are used to diagnose the model's error assumptions.
Graph of residuals against fitted values or predictors used to examine patterns and changing spread that may indicate model problems.
Regression slope expressed on standardized variable scales rather than original measurement units. Notation: β.
Regression slope expressed in the original response and predictor units. Also called B.
Applying a function, such as a logarithm or square root, to a variable to improve the suitability of a model's form or error assumptions.
Measure of how much a coefficient estimate's variance is increased by linear dependence of its predictor on the other predictors. Abbreviated VIF.
